questions.prompt: The brief needs the coffee beans in close, sharp detail. Which lens word fits best?

options.text: Wide-angle, to show more of the room
options.explanation: Imagen's guide lists wide-angle for landscapes and astronomy: big spaces, not close detail.

options.text: Macro, for close detail of small things
options.explanation: Right. Imagen's guide lists macro for food, insects and plants, and Gemini's guide names the "macro shot".

options.text: Telephoto zoom, for far, moving subjects
options.explanation: Imagen's guide lists telephoto zoom for sports and wildlife, where the subject is far away.

questions.prompt: What does OpenAI's prompting guide say about camera words like "50mm lens"?

options.text: They are cues for appearance, not a guarantee of exact physical simulation.
options.explanation: Right. A lens word asks for a look. It does not make the model act like a real lens.

options.text: They make the model simulate the real lens exactly, like a camera would do.
options.explanation: The guide says the opposite: they are cues, not a guarantee.

options.text: They are ignored by the model, so it is better to leave them out of a prompt.
options.explanation: The guide's own photo example uses "a 50mm lens". They are cues for the look.

questions.prompt: Where do you set the aspect ratio on Gemini's image models?

options.text: In the size parameter, as width x height in pixels, like 1536x1024
options.explanation: That is OpenAI's way. Gemini uses an aspect_ratio field.

options.text: In the aspect_ratio field under response_format, when its type is image
options.explanation: Right. Gemini's docs set aspect_ratio and image_size under response_format.

options.text: Nowhere: Gemini only makes squares, and you must crop every image yourself
options.explanation: Gemini lists many ratios. Its default is 1:1 only when there is no input image.
